title: Best in Class Content
article_body:
When buyers are in research mode, one of the most common things they do is search for the best option available. Best plumber near me. Top-rated project management software. Most reliable HVAC brand. Best CRM for small businesses. This behavior is universal, and it's not going away. Buyers use superlatives to orient themselves in a landscape of options, and the brands that show up for those searches are the ones that lead the conversation.

Most companies avoid this category of content for the same reason they avoid comparison content: they don't want to name competitors, and they worry about appearing self-promotional. So they stay quiet. And every day, buyers search for "best [what they sell]" and find content produced by someone else — a media outlet, a review site, or a competitor willing to participate.

## The Scope of Best-in-Class Searches

The word "best" is just the most obvious trigger. Buyers use a wide range of superlatives when researching options: most reliable, highest rated, lowest maintenance, fastest to install, safest, longest-lasting, cheapest without sacrificing quality. Any of these patterns can anchor a piece of content that captures buyers at exactly the right moment in their research process.

Yale Appliance, featured in the introduction to this methodology, built a massive content library around exactly these searches. Their article and video series on the least serviced, most reliable appliance brands attracted buyers who were doing exactly this kind of research — trying to find the right answer before making a significant purchase. That content positioned Yale as the most knowledgeable source in their market.

## The Million-Dollar Article That Named Competitors

Marcus Sheridan had just lost a sales appointment to a couple in Richmond, Virginia who wanted to see a few more pool companies before deciding. On the drive home, he realized they had essentially asked him: "Who are the best pool builders in Richmond?" So he went home and wrote exactly that article.

He listed five pool builders in Richmond. He chose them because they were the companies he'd lost the most deals to over the years. He didn't include his own company on the list, deliberately avoiding any appearance of bias. His partners thought he had lost his mind.

The result: the article has since generated more than $1 million in revenue for his company. It ranked not just for "best pool builders in Richmond" but also for several of the competitors' keywords. One customer told him directly: "I was about to sign with one of the companies on your list. I stumbled across your article. I thought, 'These guys are so honest, I should call them too.' Then I bought a pool from you."

The insight is simple: buyers are going to find a best-of list one way or another. If you're the company that publishes it — honestly, with real evaluations — you become the most trusted voice in the conversation, even if your own company isn't at the top of the list.

## Best-in-Class Content and AI Recommendations

AI models are increasingly drawing on best-of lists and ranking content when generating recommendations for users. When someone asks an AI assistant "What's the best option for X?" the AI needs sources to draw from. Companies with a strong library of honest best-in-class content are better positioned to be cited by those systems.

This introduces a balance to navigate. You want your content to be useful to AI as a source of genuine recommendations, which means it needs to be honest rather than self-promotional. A best-of list that evaluates the real landscape of options will be treated as a credible source. A list that's obviously designed to promote your own company will not.

## How to Start with Best-in-Class Content

Begin with the superlative questions your buyers are already asking. Your sales team will know these: "Who's the best [type of company] in [city]?" or "What's the best [product category] for [specific need]?" These are often the questions prospects ask at the end of a sales call, right before they say they want to look at a few more options.

Build content that genuinely answers those questions. Give real evaluations. Name options. Explain what makes each one appropriate for different buyers and situations. Use your expertise to provide context buyers can't easily find elsewhere.

Done well, best-in-class content captures buyers at the highest point of their research intensity — the moment they're actively trying to figure out who to trust. That's exactly the moment you want to be the voice they find.

what_youll_learn: Buyers instinctively search for the best, highest-rated, most reliable, or top-performing option. This behavior is universal.

You don't always have to include yourself in a best-of list to benefit. Being the company that educates buyers on the landscape builds authority regardless.
Marcus Sheridan wrote an article on the best pool builders in Richmond without including his own company, and it generated more than $1 million in revenue.

key_questions.question: Should we include our own company in best-of lists we publish?
key_questions.answer: Use judgment. Marcus Sheridan originally left his own company off best-of lists to avoid appearing biased, and it worked extremely well. As AI increasingly draws on these lists for recommendations, there may be cases where including yourself with honest context is appropriate. The test is whether your inclusion serves the buyer's understanding or just your promotion.

key_questions.question: What if we're not actually the best option in every category?
key_questions.answer: Good best-in-class content doesn't require you to win every comparison. It requires you to be honest about what each option is best for. If a competitor's product is genuinely better for a specific use case, say so. That honesty is what makes the content credible.

key_questions.question: What kinds of best-in-class content should we start with?
key_questions.answer: Start with the questions your sales team hears most: 'Who are the best [type of company] in [location]?' and 'What is the best [product type] for [specific need]?' These are the searches buyers are already running, and most companies won't touch them.

key_questions.question: Does best-in-class content work for service businesses?
key_questions.answer: Yes. In fact, service businesses often find it especially effective because most competitors refuse to participate. A law firm, accounting practice, or consulting firm that creates honest comparative content about top options in their category stands out dramatically.

key_questions.question: How does this content perform with AI search?
key_questions.answer: Very well. AI models are increasingly trained to draw on comparative and ranking content when users ask for recommendations. A strong library of best-in-class content makes your site a more authoritative source for AI to cite.
